title: Nitrogen addition raised the community temperature index in the Jasper Ridge grassland experiment in 2010-2014
abstract: We tested whether nitrogen and water supply changed thermal community sorting in the Jasper Ridge grassland experiment. We used 32 circles and 128 subplots from a fixed external data release, with 1998 baseline values and 16 treatment years. In 2010-2014, added nitrogen raised abundance-weighted community temperature index by 0.124 C (95% interval 0.054 to 0.194) and lowered community precipitation index by 17.4 mm (9.5 to 25.4). Added heat gave changes of 0.148 C and -19.4 mm. A paired nitrogen comparison after subtraction of the baseline difference gave 0.114 C (0.026 to 0.202), and 0.153 C (0.026 to 0.280) in circles without added heat. Nitrogen can therefore give a warming-like index change without added heat. Planned tests of nitrogen and water effects on the heating response were uncertain after two-test adjustment. Equal-species nitrogen change from baseline was also uncertain. The result tests the specificity of thermal indices; it does not estimate a spatial benchmark or explain a share of the global tracking gap. One annual grassland, large nutrient inputs, fire, incomplete niche coverage and missing spatial block labels limit wider use. The package contains original code, aggregate results, checks, a figure and an external-data retrieval recipe.

display.caption: Nitrogen and heating effects on community indices. Panel A shows baseline-adjusted circle models. Panel B shows paired nitrogen effects on change from 1998. Panel C shows the CTI and CPI directions in 2010-2014. Bars are pointwise 95% intervals; phases share plots.
